principles.title: Proto-Typed — describe interfaces, see prototypes, iterate with AI.
principles.description: A textual prototyping format: you write what the interface is (screens, lists, buttons, navigation) and the system takes care of the rest — no dragging blocks, no JSX, no friction.

hero.title: Proto-Typed — describe interfaces, see prototypes, iterate with AI.
hero.description: A textual prototyping format: you write what the interface is (screens, lists, buttons, navigation) and the system takes care of the rest — no dragging blocks, no JSX, no friction.
hero.highlight1_description: You describe the interface and the system takes care of the rest.
hero.highlight2_description: Cards, lists, and flows with good visual decisions by default.
hero.highlight3_description: Stable syntax for humans and models to iterate with confidence.
hero.magic_value_text: From concept to prototype in minutes. Instead of "asking for a change" in the UI, you describe the change. Instead of tweaking pixel by pixel, you rewrite the section or ask an AI to do it. The draft is always updatable and shareable.
hero.flow_describe_desc: Capture screens, lists, and actions in readable and versionable text.
hero.flow_visualize_desc: Generate navigable prototypes with consistent patterns immediately.
hero.flow_iterate_desc: Request adjustments in natural language and let AI rewrite sections.
hero.flow_export_desc: Take HTML today and open doors to other runtimes tomorrow.

context.title: The problem and the textual format
context.problem_text1: Creating UIs is still heavy: graphical tools are great for drawing, but slow to iterate; code is precise, but verbose. And AIs understand intentions, but don't "edit" visual files fluidly.
context.problem_text2: Proto-Typed was born to be the common language of prototyping between people and AIs — fast to write, easy to read, and simple to version.
context.what_is_text1: Proto-Typed is a textual interface format. You describe content, structure, and actions; it generates a navigable prototype.
context.what_is_text2: Key thinking: you focus on the intention (what is a "card", a "header", a "list"), and the system decides how to render with good defaults. It's the logic of "content first, appearance later" — like in scientific text editors — applied to UI.

process.title: How it works
process.subtitle: Describe → Visualize → Iterate → Export.
process.description: Underneath, there's a semantic representation of the interface (a "tree" that understands what a screen, card, list is). Today we render in HTML; tomorrow, React Native/Flutter and other targets. The rendering destination is secondary: priority to editing fluidity and iteration speed.

principles.title: Principles guiding Proto-Typed
principles.description: The fundamental decisions behind the textual format.
principles.principle1: Simplicity over extreme customization. Good decisions by default.
principles.principle2: Semantics before appearance. You describe "what it is"; the system chooses "how it looks".
principles.principle3: AI-friendly. Short, predictable syntax that's easy for models to generate.
principles.principle4: Portable by design. A single semantic model, multiple renderers.
principles.principle5: Cover ~90% of cases. Focus on what unlocks prototyping.

influences.title: Influences and design choices
influences.influence1_body: Inspired by TanStack Query patterns: show something now and refine later. In prototypes, this becomes "see fast, improve soon after".
influences.influence2_body: Remix's progressive enhancement philosophy guides our robustness: essential content and behavior work first, the rest is incremental improvement.
influences.influence3_heading: Hybrid by nature, choose the best place to execute.
influences.influence3_body: From Next.js, we inherit the idea of multiple rendering strategies. In Proto-Typed, it means emitting the same intention to different runtimes without rewriting.

example.title: What you write (short example)
example.result_text: What you get: a navigable prototype with layout and style patterns; ask the AI to "duplicate the metrics card" or "change the button to large secondary" and see the change in seconds.

manifesto.title: Vision manifesto (summary)
manifesto.point1: Why it exists: prototyping interfaces shouldn't require dragging boxes, memorizing frameworks, or translating intentions to pixels. Most UIs repeat predictable patterns; what changes is content, flow, and intention.
manifesto.point2: What it does: transforms these patterns into clear descriptions, readable by humans and AIs, shortening the path between idea and navigable interface.
manifesto.point3: How it does it: covers ~90% of cases with canonical layouts and semantic components, favoring fluid and natural editing, with a model decoupled from the rendering destination.
manifesto.point4: Where it's going: truly fluid human-AI co-creation — describe, visualize, request adjustments, version, and export to multiple targets without friction.

architecture.title: Interface text → Semantic representation → Renderer(s).
architecture.description: The "tree" represents interface, not HTML. This allows adding new destinations (e.g.: mobile) without changing the original description — the same separation between intention and execution that we see in modern frameworks.
architecture.item1_description: Everything starts by describing the experience in structured natural language.
architecture.item2_description: We transform the text into a "tree" that understands screens, cards, and lists — interface, not HTML.
architecture.item3_description: Today we render in HTML; tomorrow, React Native/Flutter and other targets, without changing the original description.

future.title: Where Proto-Typed is heading
future.item1: Increasingly fluid human-AI co-creation: describe, visualize, adjust through conversation.
future.item2: Multi-target rendering: HTML today; React Native/Flutter tomorrow — a single source of truth.
future.item3: Richer interaction patterns: dynamic lists, loading states, flows, and validations — in the same language.

faq.title: FAQ (quick philosophy)
faq.a1: No. We cover the space of fast textual prototyping and intention communication. Visual tools remain great for refinement and pixel-perfection.
faq.a2: Because it's editable, versionable, and conversable — by people and AIs. Iteration becomes language, not clicks.
faq.q3: Where does real data come in?
faq.a3: When necessary, you can simulate data or connect external sources in the renderers — keeping the focus on UI intention. The general philosophy is "show something now, refine later".
